transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Arcadia Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Platform), Sara Lopez (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Discussed POC guardrails and scope, credits vs committed capacity, success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), sample bench plan, and procurement next steps.

[00:00] Lena Park: All right thanks everyone for joining. Quick check in, can you hear me?
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: Yes, hear you. Thanks Lena. We're excited to get into the pilot guardrails.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Hi all, Tom here. We'll be the infra contact for the benchmark runs.
[00:20] Lena Park: Great. Agenda — go over the pilot commercial guardrails (credits, length, termination), scope of benchmarks (throughput, p99 latency, quality regressions), and procurement path. Marco will walk technical benchmark plan.
[00:35] Marco Chen: Cool. I wanna set expectations — based on what you told us in the intake, you've got a mixed workload: 60% short-chat style prompts (avg tokens 40) and 40% longer summarization jobs (avg tokens 700). Is that still accurate?
[00:50] Priya Kapoor: That's accurate. Also, the summarization jobs often have multiple continuity prompts — so KV cache matters, we saw big perf diffs in our internal tests.
[01:05] Marco Chen: Right, KV cache is a big one. For the pilot we usually recommend two axes: throughput (req/s and tokens/s) and quality (ROUGE-ish or custom scoring against your golden outputs). We'll run both hosted and a dedicated on-reserve profile if you want to compare.
[01:25] Priya Kapoor: We care about latency p95/p99 for the chat flows — anything above 400ms p95 is kinda a no-go for the UX team. For batch summarization, higher latency is fine but cost per doc matters.
[01:40] Lena Park: On credits, our standard pilot package is a named credit pool — typically 200k token-equivalents for a 6-week pilot, with an option for extension or conversion to reserved capacity. But we can tailor based on projected token volume.
[01:55] Sara Lopez: Can you summarize what happens if we blow through credits early? Is there an overage rate? And what are the termination clauses if the pilot fails?
[02:08] Lena Park: Good Q. Overage is allowed at a capped rate — we propose a temporarily higher per-token rate during the pilot which we cap in the doc. If the pilot is ended early, credits expire after 30 days unless you elect to convert to a contract. We try to avoid surprise bills; we'll set alerts and hard caps.
[02:22] Sara Lopez: Okay that sounds reasonable. We'll need the exact numbers for procurement.
[02:30] Tom Reynolds: Also curious about model variants — do you match the same model architecture for hosted vs dedicated? We need parity for benchmarking.
[02:40] Marco Chen: We map to compatible model variants. For example, if you run a 13B quantized on hosted we can spin a dedicated 13B int8 variant. There may be slight perf deltas based on kernel choices, but we surface those in the report.
[02:55] Priya Kapoor: For success criteria, internally we think: 1) p99 latency for chat < 700ms and p95 < 400ms; 2) summarization quality within 2% of our golden set (precision/recall style); 3) cost per 1k tokens below X which we'll define after you see our traffic pattern.
[03:15] Lena Park: Good — we'll capture that as the official pilot success criteria. Marco, on the bench runs, propose we do a ramp test: baseline (no batching), production-like traffic replay, and stress (2x expected QPS) to test fallbacks.
[03:32] Marco Chen: Yep. We'll also test prefix caching (they said KV cash earlier in notes) and batching policies. Quick note — sometimes our transcripts mis-spell KV cache as KV cash, ha.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: (laughs) yes we saw that in your intake sheet. One more security gating point: we need SOC2, support for our KMS, and audit logs for all inference requests. Data residency in the us-east region is preferred.
[03:57] Lena Park: Redwood supports SOC two and KMS integrations; for pilots we can provide masked logs and a private VPC path if you prefer. That will affect the onboarding lead time if you go private.
[04:12] Tom Reynolds: How long is the onboarding if we need VPC/private install? We're trying to align with our November procurement window.
[04:20] Marco Chen: For private it's usually 3–6 weeks depending on networking and certificate exchange, but for a hosted pilot with VPC peering it can be 5–10 business days. We should surface both timelines in the procurement packet.
[04:34] Sara Lopez: Procurement question — what triggers contracting? Is it usage thresholds or successful metrics? We want a clear gating that moves us from pilot credits to reserved capacity.
[04:46] Lena Park: Typical path: pilot -> milestone review -> term sheet. Milestones usually are the success criteria we agreed (latency/quality/cost). If met, Redwood issues an SOW for reserved capacity and we start commercial negotiations. We can include an option to convert leftover credits to the first month of reserved capacity to avoid waste.
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: That conversion option is appealing. Can we see an example SOW or previous pilot case study that shows conversion?
[05:13] Lena Park: We'll share a redacted SOW and a one-pager case study. I'll add that to the packet.
[05:20] Marco Chen: Back to benchmarks — we'll need two representative prompt sets from you: one for chat (short prompts) and one for summarization (long context). Also, please include golden outputs and 3 negative examples where the model should fail fast.
[05:36] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide those. Also, for the summarization jobs, we often use natively chunked inputs to keep token window reasonable; include that in the harness.
[05:45] Marco Chen: We'll replicate chunking logic. For metrics we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, reqs/sec, memory spill events, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/custom). We'll also include cost per 1k tokens estimate across batching configs.
[06:05] Tom Reynolds: Are you doing any regression detection? We need to avoid quality regressions when you switch model variants or quantization.
[06:12] Marco Chen: Yes, part of Redwood Optimize is guardrails — we'll snapshot outputs and run automatic diffs against golden outputs, produce a quality delta report. If regression exceeds threshold, we flag and recommend rollback or different quant.
[06:27] Priya Kapoor: Great. On the pilot credits: can you propose tiers? Like small (100k tokens), medium (300k), large (1M) with respective price points and extension discounts?
[06:38] Lena Park: Yes. We'll propose a tailored tier table in the credit proposal doc. Also propose an overage cap and an option to pre-buy reserved units if you expect steady usage.
[06:48] Sara Lopez: For procurement, we'll need the following in writing: payment terms, indemnity language, data handling and deletion policy, and SSO/SAML support. Also please include an estimate for any professional services for private setup.
[07:02] Lena Park: Understood. We'll include PS estimates and a clear travel of responsibilities doc.
[07:08] Priya Kapoor: One more technical: can the benchmark harness produce per-model memory traces? We want to see GPU utilization patterns.
[07:17] Marco Chen: Yes we'll include GPU utilization, kernel-level perf counters where available, and a heatmap of sequence-length distribution vs latency. There may be sampling noise but it's useful.
[07:30] Tom Reynolds: If dedicated reserved capacity is needed, what's the lead time for GPUs? We might need guaranteed throughput for 24/7 jobs.
[07:39] Lena Park: For reserved it's typically 2–4 weeks provisioning depending on region and instance type. For urgent needs we offer burst capacity options during the first 30 days of a commitment.
[07:51] Sara Lopez: That helps. Can we get a sample pilot contract with termination language? Also, will you provide a PO-ready invoice for pilot credits?
[08:02] Lena Park: Yes we'll provide a sample pilot addendum and a PO-ready invoice template.
[08:10] Priya Kapoor: For success metrics again — let's lock p95 < 400ms chat, p99 < 700ms chat, summarization quality within 2% of golden set, and cost per doc target TBD after you see our traffic envelope.
[08:27] Lena Park: Locked that in. Any other questions?
[08:31] Tom Reynolds: Just timezone note — we prefer benchmarks run overnight PST so it doesn't affect our staging.
[08:38] Marco Chen: Noted, we can schedule runs.
[08:42] Sara Lopez: Procurement will check the pilot credit ranges. If the mid tier covers our expected volume we'll aim to sign pilot by Nov 14.
[08:51] Lena Park: Great. I'll send the credit proposal + pilot SOW + security one-pager by Nov 6. Marco will follow up on benchmark plan and schedule. Priya and Tom will send artifacts. Sara to send procurement timeline.
[09:05] (crosstalk) Priya Kapoor: And we'll see how the numbers look, if we need to expand credits mid-pilot we'll coordinate.
[09:12] Lena Park: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll share the packet and book the benchmark slot once artifacts are in.
[09:18] End meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional ASR errors (KV cash/KV cache, SOC two/SOC2), speaker overlap labeled as crosstalk, and some proper nouns normalized inconsistently.
